exercise.title: Major and minor ii–V–I in one tune
exercise.why: A tune can reach its major home with one ii–V–I and its minor home, on La, with another, and the ii chord says early which is coming: minor 7 before the major home, half-diminished before the minor one.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the band: a ii–V–I to C major, then a ii–V–i to A minor, round and round. Call out "major" or "minor" as each home chord arrives.
Then listen two bars earlier, to each ii chord: Dm7 before the major home, Bm7♭5 before the minor one.

Press Play below to start the band again, slower. Tap the root of each chord on the staff under the band as its box lights: {{2}}, {{5}}, {{1}}, then {{7}}, {{3}}, {{6}}.
Both lines move by the same leaps, and they end on the two ringed homes, {{1}} and {{6}}.

Press Play below to start the band. Look away from the chord boxes and call out 2, 5 or 1 on each change, and "major" or "minor" on each home chord, then look to check.
Once the ii chord tells you which home is coming, listen in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Play to start the band again.
When you change the key, the chords are new but the minor home is still the 6 of the major one.
